select_live_row_determinism.explanation: Enum.max_by(many, & &1.updated_at) uses Erlang structural map comparison for DateTime structs, NOT DateTime.compare/2. Erlang compares maps by key-value pairs in sorted atom key order. For DateTime structs the keys compare as: __struct__ < calendar < day < hour < microsecond < minute < month < second < std_offset < time_zone < utc_offset < year < zone_abbr. The :microsecond field is compared BEFORE :minute, :month, :second, :year. Consequence: if older.updated_at has a larger :microsecond value (e.g. {999900, 6}) than newer.updated_at (e.g. {9900, 6}) because the newer timestamp crossed a second boundary, the structural comparison evaluates older > newer INCORRECTLY -- the function returns the older row. This is a real defect, not a phantom.
select_live_row_determinism.reproduction_rate: RARE (~1% per run): the 10ms Process.sleep(10) window only straddles a second boundary when older.updated_at is within the last 10ms of its second (microsecond > 990000). Under targeted 15-iteration load test in ISS-0776 attempt 2, this condition was not hit by chance, which is expected at ~1% probability over 15 iterations.
select_live_row_determinism.when_many_branch_triggered: Only when candidates has > 1 element. In the test suite, only the test 'two tied live generic rows -- the most recently updated_at one wins, deterministically' triggers it: creates two live generic rows (process_definition_id nil), no process_definition_id in the request, so matching=[], candidates=[older, newer]. The 'specific outranks generic' test does NOT trigger it: matching=[specific], candidates=[specific], returns [single] branch.
select_live_row_determinism.cross_contamination_ruled_out: Yes. Per-tenant-schema isolation (each test calls TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!) means schemas are independent. Another test's rows cannot contaminate this test's candidates list.
select_live_row_determinism.pre_assertion_guard: The test asserts DateTime.compare(newer.updated_at, older.updated_at) == :gt BEFORE the HTTP call, confirming DB-stored timestamps are ordered. But this does not protect against Enum.max_by using structural comparison -- DateTime.compare uses semantic logic that Enum.max_by does not.

fix_recommendation.proposed_fix_reason: Still uses structural DateTime comparison for the first tuple element. Tuples compare element-by-element; the DateTime comparison bug applies equally to {updated_at, id} as to updated_at alone. The :id secondary sort key only helps for truly equal timestamps, not for the second-boundary inversion case.
fix_recommendation.correct_fix_reason: DateTime.to_unix/2 with :microsecond precision converts to a plain integer (microseconds since Unix epoch). Integer comparison is always correct regardless of second/minute/hour/day boundaries. The secondary &1.id tiebreaker provides full determinism for truly simultaneous timestamps. This is a one-line change at line ~183 of lib/letflow/routers/help.ex.
fix_recommendation.alternative_fix: Enum.sort_by(many, &{DateTime.to_unix(&1.updated_at, :microsecond), &1.id}, :desc) |> hd() -- equivalent correctness, but Enum.max_by with the integer conversion is simpler and O(n) vs O(n log n) for sort.
